segments.name: option
segments.comment: Configuration option where the DSU mode will be stored. There are 4 options per port.

verbo_map.comment: address generation for input buffer (cannot be active simultaneously with the output buffer)
address generation for output buffer (cannot be active simultaneously with the input buffer)

segments.name: stride
segments.comment: Offset term 0: the address is offset by stride * the loop counter named by loop_level. 0 disables it. Use evts for extra terms or for a stride too wide for this field.

segments.name: loop_level
segments.comment: Which loop level's counter drives the stride offset; 0 = outermost. The default 3 is an 'auto' sentinel the compiler resolves to the innermost enclosing loop; an explicit 0/1/2 is kept.

segments.name: port
segments.comment: The port number (must match the evt this extends).

verbo_map.comment: extends the input buffer init address
extends the output buffer init address

segments.name: init_addr_high
segments.comment: High bits above the evt init_addr field: the effective address is {init_addr_high, evt.init_addr}. Issue after the matching evt on the same port.

segments.name: port
segments.comment: The port number (must match the evt this extends).

segments.name: stride
segments.comment: Stride for one loop dimension. Wider than evt.stride, so the compiler also routes oversized evt strides here. Port offset = sum over evt + evts terms of stride * loop counter.

segments.name: loop_level
segments.comment: Which loop-nesting level's counter this stride term multiplies. 0 = outermost.

segments.name: ext
segments.comment: 0 = base (low half), 1 = extension (high MSBs) of iter/step/delay

segments.name: port
segments.comment: Select which port the repetition applies to.

segments.name: port
segments.comment: select which port the transition applies to.
